answer: A farm running 41 keys therefore pays for 41 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the hollow declaration. Because the marble audit recomputes usage from the wharf history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 845 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
